stem:
Esha sketches the stars at 8 p.m. in January. In February she compares Earth’s night sky at 8 p.m. with the sky at 2 a.m. She is deciding whether Earth’s rotation on its axis or Earth’s revolution around the Sun explains the month-to-month change at the same clock time.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The change from January’s 8 p.m. sky to February’s 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s revolution around the Sun.
The entire difference between January’s 8 p.m. sky and February’s 2 a.m. sky is caused by Earth’s revolution.
The change from January’s 8 p.m. sky to February’s 8 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s rotation on its axis.
Earth’s rotation and revolution are the same motion, so either word explains the February 8 p.m. change.

teacher.key_rationale: Month-to-month change at the same clock time traces to Earth’s revolution. Comparing January 8 p.m. with February 2 a.m. mixes daily turning with orbital change; rotation alone does not explain that fixed-time shift; rotation and revolution are different motions.
